title: Tale of King Ins bin Kays and His Daughter

full_text:
King Ins bin Kays of ancient Yemen faced a severe economic crisis: a prolonged drought had dried the mountain streams, trade caravans were avoiding the kingdom, and the royal council proposed doubling the taxes on the impoverished farmers.

The king’s daughter, Princess Bilqis, who had studied agriculture and maritime commerce, stepped before the royal throne:

'Sire, doubling taxes on starving farmers is like milking a dead goat! You will provoke rebellion and destroy the kingdom.

Let us instead open the royal reserves of grain to feed the peasants, employ twenty thousand laborers to construct three stone dams in the mountain gorges to catch the winter floods, and reduce import duties at our port of Aden to attract the merchant fleets of India!'

The king adopted his daughter’s strategic vision.

Within three years, the stone dams captured the mountain waters, green fields of sugarcane and cotton bloomed across the valley, and Aden became the wealthiest port in the Arabian Sea!

King Ins bin Kays proclaimed his daughter Crown Princess and Chief Minister, teaching all monarchs that wisdom and visionary governance are gifts that elevate a realm.
moral: A ruler who empowers wise counsel regardless of gender preserves his realm from economic ruin.
